title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

errors: No mathematical error. Implicit hypotheses: S affine (or the statement localised); A -> A_n injective (U schematically dense in S, e.g. S flat over Z), so that 'extension' is unique; B finitely generated, so that finitely many coefficients need clearing.
Necessity is immediate (evaluate at 0). The reduction from group homomorphism to morphism of schemes relies on the density argument of the previous page, which is fine for S flat with U dense.

ideas.what: A morphism G_{a,U} -> G_U over U = S[1/n] extends to S after precomposition with multiplication by n^nu if and only if u(0) extends. Hence every homomorphism G_a -> G defined away from n becomes integral after rescaling.
ideas.modern_name: Clearing denominators / integral structures on homomorphisms from G_a (integral lattices in Lie algebras, integral exponential maps)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore (standard in the theory of group schemes over Dedekind bases; cf. Bruhat–Tits-type integral models)

ideas.what: Attaching to an extension 1->M->𝔊->H->1 of discrete groups (M free abelian of finite type) a group scheme over Z: the pushout of the constant group 𝔊_Z along M -> M ⊗ G_a. Its Z-points recover 𝔊. There is also a pro-group scheme built from the finite-index sublattices of M.
ideas.modern_name: Relative / weighted completion of discrete groups, integral form (vector-group extension of a constant group)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Hain (relative completion, 1990s); Hain–Matsumoto (weighted completion, 2003); Deligne (unipotent/motivic fundamental groups, 1989)
ideas.where_published: Only in the unpublished Longue Marche continuation (Montpellier cote 140-4)

missed.claim: Grothendieck sketches a schematisation over Z of discrete group extensions with free abelian kernel: a vector-group extension of a constant group, plus a pro-version indexed by finite-index sublattices. The integrality lemma for G_a-homomorphisms is used to control denominators. This anticipates integral versions of relative completion of (e.g. mapping class / Galois-type) groups. Integral (as opposed to Q-) structures there are still relatively little developed.
missed.quote: Soit maintenant M un Z-module libre de type fini, on va construire un pro-schéma en groupes sur S, associé au syst. projectif des sous-Z-modules d'indice fini de M
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Integral and p-adic models of relative completions of arithmetic fundamental groups, and comparison between profinite and schematic completions over Z, are active questions. Grothendieck's lattice-indexed pro-system is one explicit way to mediate between them.

deep.surprise_reason: The lemma itself is routine. Its interest lies in context: an unpublished 1981 attempt to build integral group-scheme models of discrete group extensions, a precursor of relative/weighted completion, with an integral pro-structure that is not standard in the literature.
transcription_corrections: '$\pi_1^{t}(u)$' / '$\pi_1^{t}$' is almost certainly 'u(0)' (the value of u at the origin of E^1), matching a_0 in (25).
'une puissance n-ième de u' should read roughly 'une puissance n^ν de n telle que u∘φ_{n^ν} (φ_m donné par (24)) se prolonge'.
'E^1_U' denotes the affine line / additive group G_a over U.
'théorème du site p. 662'' is uncertain; it refers to a 'théorème' stated on p. 662' (the reading 'du site' is doubtful).
Margin note: 'Schémas en groupes associés aux ext. des groupes discrets'.
